Surah 97: Al-Qadr (The Night of Decree)

Makki, though it is also said to be Madani; its verses number 5. [It was revealed after ʿAbasa.] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Qur'an is magnified in three respects. First: its revelation is attributed to Allah Himself, and it is singled out as belonging to Him alone, not to anyone else.

Second: it came with a pronoun rather than with its explicit name, as a testimony to its eminence and a sufficiency that needs no pointing out.

Third: the elevation of the time in which it was sent down. It is related that it was sent down all at once, on the Night of Decree (laylat al-Qadr), from the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) to the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya). Jibril dictated it to the scribes (al-safara), and then he would bring it down upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in installments over twenty-three years. It is also related from al-Sha'bi: the meaning is that We began its revelation on the Night of Decree.

They differed about the time of that night. Most of them hold that it is in the month of Ramadan, in the last ten nights, on its odd nights, and the most common view is that it is the seventh of them. Perhaps the reason it was concealed is that whoever seeks it may stay awake many nights, hoping to coincide with it, so that his worship multiplies and his reward is doubled; and that people, upon its being made known, should not rely on attaining its merit and neglect other nights.

The meaning of laylat al-Qadr is the night of the determination and decree of affairs, from His words, exalted is He: ﴿In it every wise affair is made distinct﴾. It is also said it was so named for its importance and nobility over all other nights. ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?﴾ That is: your understanding does not reach the extent of its virtue and the limit of its exalted rank. Then He explained it: it is better than a thousand months. The cause of its virtue reaching this degree is the religious benefits found in it, which were mentioned: the descent of the angels and the Spirit, and the decision of every wise affair.

Regarding the specification of this period, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who carried weapons in the way of Allah for a thousand months, so the believers marveled at that and felt their own deeds to be small, so they were given a night better than the duration of that warrior [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and others, through Ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, as a mursal report, without his words "and their deeds seemed small to them."]]. It is also said: in former times a man would not be called an ʿabid (worshipper) until he had worshipped Allah for a thousand months; so they were given a night which, if they kept it awake, made them more deserving of being called worshippers than those worshippers.

﴿The angels and the Spirit descend﴾ to the lowest heaven. It is also said: to the earth. ﴿The Spirit﴾ is Jibril. It is also said: a kind of angel whom the angels do not see except on that night. ﴿With every decree﴾: they descend because of every matter Allah has decreed for that year until the next. It is also read: "from every man" (min kulli amri'), meaning on account of every person. It is said: they do not meet a believing man or woman except that they greet him on that night. ﴿Peace it is, until the rising of the dawn﴾: that is, it is nothing but safety, meaning Allah decrees in it only safety and good, while in other nights He decrees trials and safety. Or: it is nothing but greeting, because of how much they greet the believers. It is also read "maṭlaʿ" with the lam vowelled with fatha and with kasra.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites the Surah of Al-Qadr is given a reward like one who fasted Ramadan and stood in vigil on the Night of Decree."
[[Narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]]
